svg.title: Deploy $12,000–$65,000 Without Buying a Fleet
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Deploy $12,000–$65,000 Without Buying a Fleet; subtitle: Four capital buckets; the rendered example totals $35,000.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values are USD allocations for one $35,000 startup stack. Low-envelope allocations total $12,000; high-envelope allocations total $65,000. Endpoint allocations are coordinated budgets, not independently selectable cost ranges. This model assumes investor-supplied vehicles and excludes vehicle acquisitions.; caption: Example: $10,000 + $5,000 + $8,000 + $12,000 = $35,000. Low envelope: $4,000 + $1,500 + $2,500 + $4,000 = $12,000. High envelope: $20,000 + $8,000 + $12,000 + $25,000 = $65,000. Startup cash, refundable deposits, and operating expense are different ledger categories.; stages: label: Insurance and authority funding; value: $10,000 example allocation for coverage activation and operating credentials; numeric value: 10000.0; detail: Allocate $4,000 in the low envelope and $20,000 in the high envelope for required insurance deposits, initial premiums, inspections, and applicable authority fees. Obtain actual quotes before accepting vehicle commitments.; label: Telematics and collection infrastructure; value: $5,000 example allocation for installed monitoring and billing setup; numeric value: 5000.0; detail: Allocate $1,500 low and $8,000 high for OBD-II devices, GPS installation, secure account setup, collection integration, and settlement templates. Treat later subscriptions as operating costs rather than repeatedly charging them to startup capital.; label: Contracts and vehicle onboarding; value: $8,000 example allocation for documented vehicle and driver activation; numeric value: 8000.0; detail: Allocate $2,500 low and $12,000 high for contract drafting, authorized screening, condition documentation, initial preparation, and handover logistics. Exclude vehicle purchase prices and investor capital contributions.; label: Liquidity and collision buffer; value: $12,000 example allocation retained as operating liquidity; numeric value: 12000.0; detail: Allocate $4,000 low and $25,000 high for deductible liquidity, collection delays, and service interruptions. Keep customer deposits separate. Holding this cash does not reduce accounting profit; recognized expenses and actual disbursements follow their own timing.

rect.title: label: Insurance and authority funding; numeric value: 10000.0; value: $10,000 example allocation for coverage activation and operating credentials; detail: Allocate $4,000 in the low envelope and $20,000 in the high envelope for required insurance deposits, initial premiums, inspections, and applicable authority fees. Obtain actual quotes before accepting vehicle commitments.
